ms.promise: Write a specification of validator that will be later implemented in various languages to compare their performance.
ms.criteria: Specification document that provides a high level overview of the protocol, fully describes design and required checks of the validator is published.
ms.report:
Outputs:
Validator specifications written in LaTeX describing validators to be implemented later in various languages to compare performance as outlined in our SoM.

Acceptance:
Our specification document provides the high-level protocol overview and explanation of the validator design and checks as outlined in our SoM.

Evidence:

Evergreen specification documents for project validators written in LaTeX
https://mlabs-haskell.github.io/uplc-benchmark/specifications.html

And the LaTeX code is hosted in a GH repo
https://github.com/mlabs-haskell/uplc-benchmark/tree/master/specifications

ms.promise: Implement a validator specified in the document from milestone one in Plutarch.
ms.criteria: The implemented Plutarch validator matches the high-level overview from the specification document and implemented validator checks match the technical specification.
ms.report:
OUTPUTS
Using the LaTeX validator specification delivered in milestone one, team members were able to quickly implement our milestone two delivery, a Plutarch implementation. Due to our quick pace of delivery - and adjusted for staffing concerns around the holiday season - the implementation was actually delivered notably ahead of schedule (merged Dec 11th). Nevertheless, this is the deliverable detailed in our original Ideascale proposal and our milestone two statement document.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA 
As can be seen in the PR linked below, the merge contains several configuration and build management files and, more importantly, source code files for the Plutarch implementation. As described in the LaTeX specification file delivered as part of our first Proof of Achievement, the Haskell files contain the implementation of a validator script - written using Plutarch - for a simple example protocol, an NFT marketplace. The reader will recall that this example protocol will be implemented in several on-chain languages and benchmarked to identify the most performant languages.

Per the Acceptance criteria of our Milestone Two documentation, developers have ensured this Plutarch implementation matches the specification design and implemented validator checks that match the technical specification as well.

EVIDENCE
The files comprising the completion of this milestone, and our proof of achievement can be found here
https://github.com/mlabs-haskell/uplc-benchmark/pull/13/files
And which we are happy to say we were able to deliver ahead of schedule owing to the hard work of our team members.
